common.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
common.moreMatches: {{count}} more: type more to narrow the list

home.degraded: System status: the database is not reachable

login.title: Sign in
login.codeHelp: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.

twoFactor.title: Set up two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.help: Your role needs a second step when signing in. Scan this code with an authenticator app (such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator), then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
twoFactor.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
twoFactor.manual: Can't scan? Enter this key in the app:
twoFactor.recoveryHelp: If you lose your phone, each of these codes lets you sign in once. Print them or store them somewhere safe. They will not be shown again.

password.title: Change password
password.firstTime: Please choose your own password before continuing.
password.rules: At least 10 characters. Avoid common words, only numbers, or anything close to your name or email.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.

users.title: Users
users.created: Account created for {{email}}. Give them this temporary password (it is shown only once); they must change it at first sign-in:
users.thenActivate: The account stays switched off until you give it roles and divisions and activate it.

access.ownAccount: This is your own account. Another administrator must change your access.
access.savedWithWarnings: Saved. The conflict and your reason have been recorded.
access.legend: ● from roles   + granted for this user   − removed for this user   … waiting for the Director. Click a cell to grant or remove.
access.waitingForDirector: This is sensitive access: it takes effect once the Director confirms it.
access.noOverrides: None. This user has exactly their roles' access.

review.title: Access review {{period}}
review.help: Check that each person's access is still right for their job. Rows with sensitive access still waiting for confirmation are highlighted.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.help: Every change to users, roles, access and settings: who, when, from where, the old and new values, and why. Nobody can edit or delete it.

event.division_first_used: Division first used on a document
event.quotation_limit_confirmed: Quotation limits confirmed by the Director
event.payee_bank_change_acknowledged: Changed bank details checked by the Accountant
event.document_sent_down: Document changed and sent back a level
event.voucher_amended: Amendment of an approved voucher started

company.title: Company profile
company.help: The company's details, printed on vouchers and other documents.
company.baseCurrencyFixed: Every amount in the books is in this currency, so it cannot be changed.
company.logoRules: PNG or JPEG, 1 MB at most.

divisions.title: Divisions
divisions.help: Every voucher, ledger line and report carries a division. A division added here can be used straight away. Once a division has been used on a document its code is fixed, and it can only be deactivated, not deleted.
divisions.name: Name
divisions.created: Division {{code}} {{name}} added. It can be used straight away.
divisions.codeHelp: The code is two letters or digits, for example WS. It is the first part of every voucher number of this division.
divisions.lockedHelp: This division has been used on documents, so its code cannot change.
divisions.reasonNeeded: To deactivate or delete, give a reason first.
divisions.taxInvoiceCodeHelp: The division's code in tax invoice numbers, e.g. W1 in 26SEP_W1_35: 1 to 15 letters or digits.
divisions.taxInvoiceCodeLocked: This tax invoice code has been used on invoices, so it cannot change.

numbering.title: Number series
numbering.help: How each kind of document is numbered. Vouchers: {PP}{YY}{MM}{DD}{XXX}, e.g. IM261023003. Tax invoices follow the government format YYMMM_code_serial: {YY}{MMM}_{IC}_{XX}, e.g. 26SEP_W1_35, restarting at 01 each month for each division.
numbering.tokens: Click to add: {PP} division code, {IC} division's tax invoice code, {YY} or {YYYY} year, {MM} month number or {MMM} month letters (SEP), {DD} day, {XX} running number (one X per digit, at least). Letters, digits and - / . _ can go between them.
numbering.neverReused: Numbers already given are never given again, even after a change.
numbering.whenFull: When the running number is full

whenFullOptions.stop: Stop and ask the Admin to widen it

factory.title: Divisions, sections and machines
factory.help: The factory structure used by entry pages, plans, costing and reports. Choose a section or machine in the tree to see or change it. Codes are fixed once used on a transaction; anything with history is made inactive or retired instead of deleted.
factory.pick: Choose a section or machine in the tree, or add one.
factory.codeFixed: This has been used on transactions, so its code cannot change and it cannot be deleted.
factory.reasonNeeded: To make inactive or delete, give a reason first.
factory.retireHelp: To retire a machine, set its status to Retired and give a reason. Retired machines leave the entry pages; their history stays.
factory.ratesHelp: A new rate applies from its date; earlier jobs keep the rate they had. A rate that has not started yet can be removed.
factory.uploadPhoto: Upload a photo (PNG or JPEG, 5 MB at most)
factory.importHelp: Use the layout of the export: export, edit in Excel, then import. Check the file first: nothing is saved until every row is accepted.
factory.checked: The file is fine. Importing it would add {{sections_created}} and update {{sections_updated}} sections, and add {{machines_created}} and update {{machines_updated}} machines.
factory.imported: Imported: {{sections_created}} sections added, {{sections_updated}} updated; {{machines_created}} machines added, {{machines_updated}} updated.
factory.sectionScopeHelp: Production staff can be limited to particular sections, for example a supervisor for Manual Milling. Supervisors also see the sections they supervise.

shifts.title: Shifts and rosters
shifts.help: Shifts, the rotations crews follow, and which roster is in force from which date. A night shift belongs to the date it started. Rosters are dated: to change the season, end the current roster and add a new one from a date; past days never change.
shifts.overnightHelp: This shift ends after midnight; it belongs to the date it starts.
shifts.crewMembersLater: Crew members are picked from the employee register, which comes with the HR module.
shifts.crewsStartHelp: For each crew, choose the day of the cycle it starts on, e.g. A on day 1, B on day 3, C on day 5. Leave out crews not on this roster; a roster with no crews applies to everyone (e.g. the General shift).

currencies.title: Currencies and exchange rates
currencies.help: LKR is the base currency. Documents in another currency use the rate of their date; if that day has no rate, the latest earlier rate is used and the document says so. A rate used on a document can never change.
currencies.switchHelp: To switch a currency off, give a reason first. Switched-off currencies leave the pickers on new documents.
currencies.rateHelp: LKR for one unit of the currency. If the bank quotes buying and selling, enter both and leave the rate empty: their middle is used. Correcting a saved rate needs a reason.
currencies.importHelp: Columns: date (YYYY-MM-DD), currency, rate, and optionally buying and selling. Check the file first: nothing is saved until every line is accepted.
currencies.checked: The file is fine. Importing it would add {{added}} rates, correct {{corrected}} and leave {{unchanged}} unchanged.

limits.title: Quotation approval limits
limits.help: The Director approves every quotation. A quotation below its division's minimum margin, or above its maximum value, is shown to the Director with a warning. Foreign-currency quotations are converted at the rate of their date. Changes entered by the Admin take effect only after the Director confirms them.
limits.notSetHelp: Until a division's limits are confirmed, the defaults apply: a minimum margin of 1% and no maximum value.
limits.changeText: from {{from}}, minimum margin {{margin}}, maximum value {{value}} (entered by {{by}}).
limits.proposeHelp: Old quotations keep the limits in force on their date. If the Director confirms after the start date, the limits apply from the day of confirmation.

payees.title: Suppliers and payees
payees.help: Everyone a voucher can pay: suppliers, utilities, banks and credit cards, government, employees and others. Bank details can be entered or changed only by the Accountant (or someone the Director has allowed); every change is recorded and shown to the Accountant on the payee's next voucher.
payees.bankChangedNotice: Bank details were changed by {{by}} on {{at}}. The Accountant checks them on the next voucher.
payees.confirmDuplicate: I have checked: this is a different payee. Save anyway.
payees.acknowledge: I have checked the new bank details
payees.bankChangeHelp: Every change is recorded with the old and new details and your reason, and flagged to the Accountant on the payee's next voucher.
payees.bankOnlyAccountant: Only the Accountant can enter or change bank details.

banking.title: Bank and cash accounts
banking.help: The company's bank accounts, cash and petty cash, with cheque books. Each cheque number can be used once only: issued on a payment, or recorded as spoiled with a reason. Each division has a default bank account for its payments.
banking.inUse: This account has been used: its code, bank, number and currency can no longer change.
banking.defaults: Default bank account of each division
banking.defaultsHelp: Payments of a division are made from this account unless the Cashier chooses another.
banking.ledgerHelp: The Bank-type account in the chart of accounts that this account's money is recorded in. It is needed before the account is used on payments.

chart.title: Chart of accounts
chart.help: Every amount the company records goes to one of these accounts. The type decides where the account appears on the balance sheet or the profit and loss; the detail type refines it. Sub-accounts have the same type as their parent. Numbers are optional and, when used, set the order.
chart.name: Name
chart.systemHelp: The system posts to this account, so it cannot be deleted, made inactive, merged away or given another type. It can be renamed and numbered.
chart.inUse: This account has been used: it cannot be deleted, and its number can no longer change.
chart.mergedHelp: This account was merged into {{name}}. Its entries are kept as they were posted and are reported under {{name}}.
chart.mergeHelp: Merging moves this account's history and sub-accounts to the account you choose, which must be of the same type. A merge cannot be undone. Making an account inactive also makes its sub-accounts inactive.
chart.detailTypesHelp: The list of detail types for each account type. A detail type in use can be renamed or made inactive (accounts that have it keep it), but not deleted.
chart.importHelp: One sheet named Accounts, in the layout of the export: Number, Name, Parent (written as Parent:Sub-account), Type, Detail type, Description, Default division, Active. Rows are matched by number, or else by full name. Check the file first: nothing is saved until every row is accepted.
chart.checked: The file is fine. Importing it would add {{created}} and update {{updated}} accounts ({{unchanged}} unchanged), and add {{detail_types_created}} detail types.
chart.imported: Imported: {{created}} accounts added, {{updated}} updated, {{unchanged}} unchanged; {{detail_types_created}} detail types added.

journal.title: Journal
journal.help: Every posted entry, newest first. A posted entry never changes: a mistake is corrected by reversing it, which posts the mirror entry.
journal.reverseHelp: Posts the mirror entry, dated like this one if its month is open, otherwise today. This entry stays as it is.

periods.title: Accounting periods
periods.help: Each month is open until the Director closes it. Nothing can be posted into a closed month. Reopening needs a reason and is recorded in the audit log.

matrix.title: Approval matrix
matrix.help: Who approves each kind of document, level by level. Level 1 is the person who submits. Where several rules fit a document at a level, the most specific one (division, type, amount) is used. A rule is never edited: add the new one and switch the old one off. Documents already submitted keep the route they were given.
matrix.levelOne: L1: the person who creates and submits the document.
matrix.minimum: At least {{levels}} approval levels, always ending with the Director, whatever the type or amount.

bell.settingsHelp: Choose, for each kind of event, whether it appears under the bell and whether it is also sent to your email address.

events.approval_waiting: A document is waiting for my approval
events.approval_reminder: Reminder: a document has been waiting a long time for my approval
events.document_returned: A document I created was returned to me
events.document_approved: A document I created was approved
events.document_rejected: A document I created was rejected

email.title: Send by email
email.subject: Subject
email.notReady: Document email is not set up yet. Ask the Admin to enter the sending mailbox under Settings → Document email.

documentEmail.title: Document email
documentEmail.help: The mailbox that quotations, invoices, statements, outstanding reports and other documents are emailed from, and the default message for each kind. The person sending can edit the message before it goes.
documentEmail.accountHelp: Use the finance mailbox's own mail server (for example smtp.hostinger.com, port 465 with SSL) so the company domain's SPF and DKIM records cover the emails. The password is stored encrypted and is never shown again.
documentEmail.copyTo: Send a copy of every email to (optional)

securities.none: None (only for a mail server on this machine)

documentEmail.passwordKeep: New password (leave empty to keep the saved one)
documentEmail.testOk: The last test email was sent successfully.
documentEmail.notTested: Send a test email to check these settings.
documentEmail.notReady: Not set up yet: documents cannot be emailed.
documentEmail.messagesHelp: The subject and message offered for each kind of document. Words in braces, such as {document_number}, are filled in for each email; only the placeholders listed can be used.

sentEmails.title: Sent emails
sentEmails.help: Every document and report emailed from the system, exactly as it was sent. This record cannot be changed or deleted.

taxes.title: Taxes
taxes.help: As in QuickBooks: each tax (VAT, SSCL, withholding tax…) has its rates from a date, and tax codes say which taxes a document line carries and in what order. The starting taxes are suggestions without rates: check them and enter the rates in force.
taxes.codesHelp: A tax code is chosen on each document line. Taxes in a code are charged in order; a later tax can be charged on the amount plus the taxes above it (VAT on the amount plus SSCL).
taxes.name: Name
taxes.onNetAndTax: on the amount plus the taxes above
taxes.inUse: This tax has been used on documents: its code is fixed, and a rate in force cannot change. A new rate can start today or later.
taxes.codeInUse: This tax code has been used on documents: its taxes cannot change. Make a new tax code and switch this one off.
taxes.enterRate: Enter the rate in force before this tax is used.
taxes.salesAccount: Account for tax on sales (owed to the government)
taxes.purchaseAccount: Account for tax on purchases (claimed back)
taxes.partOfCost: Not claimed back: part of the cost
taxes.taxesInCode: Taxes in this code, in order
taxes.share: Charged on (% of the amount), tax {{n}}

voucherTypes.title: Voucher types
voucherTypes.help: The kinds of payment a voucher can be. The type is a field and a list filter; it is not part of the voucher number, and every type passes the same three approval levels, ending with the Director.
voucherTypes.name: Name
voucherTypes.advance: Advance: paid before the invoice and set off against it later
voucherTypes.inUse: This type has been used on vouchers: its code and how it is paid are fixed. To change them, add a new type and switch this one off.

vouchers.title: Payment vouchers
vouchers.payeeHint: Type at least 2 letters of the name or code
vouchers.plusTaxCodes: plus the taxes worked out from the tax codes
vouchers.noFiles: No files yet. Attach the scanned invoice before submitting.
vouchers.dropHere: Drop PDF, JPG or PNG files here (20 MB at most each), or:
vouchers.submitHelp: The voucher goes to the Accountant, then the Director. It cannot be changed after this unless it is returned to you.

actions.send_down: Changed and sent back to the Accountant

vouchers.matchedInvoices: Matched supplier invoices of this payee still to pay
vouchers.matchTotals: invoice LKR {{total}}, on vouchers LKR {{onVouchers}}, due {{due}}
vouchers.advanceLine: Advance payment on a purchase order
vouchers.advanceReasonOf: Why the advance is needed, line {{n}}
vouchers.advanceReasonHint: Why it is needed (the Director approves)
vouchers.advanceOnPo: Pay an advance on a purchase order
vouchers.advanceHelp: An advance is paid only on an approved PO still waiting for goods, as an exception the Director approves. It goes to Advances to suppliers and is set off against the supplier's invoice once paid.
vouchers.noAdvanceOrders: This payee has no approved purchase order waiting for goods in this division.
vouchers.advanceException: Exception: advance of LKR {{amount}} on purchase order {{po}} (LKR {{total}}) before the goods arrive. It is set off against the supplier's invoice once paid.

voucherReview.title: Waiting for my approval
voucherReview.help: Vouchers waiting at your level, oldest first. Check the scanned invoice, give each line its account, division (or split a shared bill across divisions) and tax, then approve, return to the Clerk or reject. Return and Reject need a reason.
voucherReview.saveFirst: Approve saves the coding first. A voucher is approved at L2 only when every line has its account and division.
voucherReview.unsaved: Coding changed and not saved yet.

director.title: Approve vouchers
director.empty: No vouchers are waiting for you.
director.reasonsMissing: Give a reason for every voucher you reject (highlighted).
director.summary: Approve {{approve}} vouchers totalling LKR {{total}}, and reject {{reject}}?

voucherActions.noFiles: No files are attached to this voucher.
voucherActions.printHelp: The payment voucher opens as a PDF to print or save. Every print is logged; reprints are marked "Copy". A voucher not yet approved by the Director is marked "Not approved".
voucherActions.deleteHelp: The voucher leaves the working lists but is kept, with its files and full history, in Deleted vouchers. Its number is never used again. This cannot be undone.
voucherActions.sentBack: Changed by {{name}} and sent back for checking:
voucherActions.reviseHelp: You can correct the description here (coding is on the review page). A change to the payee, amounts or lines sends the voucher back to the Accountant, with the changes listed.
voucherActions.amendHelp: An approved voucher is never changed. A new revision is created as a draft for you to correct and submit; it goes to the Accountant and the Director again. Until it is approved the original cannot be paid; if the amendment is rejected or deleted, the original stands.
voucherActions.cancelHelp: The Director approves or rejects the cancellation. Until then the voucher cannot be amended, deleted or paid. A voucher with any payment can never be cancelled.

deletedVouchers.title: Deleted vouchers
deletedVouchers.help: Vouchers removed from the working lists, with who deleted them, when and why. Open one to see its full history.

amendments.title: Amendments
amendments.help: Revisions of approved vouchers: each one with the voucher it amends, why, and how the amount changed.
amendments.replacedBy: This voucher is replaced and cannot be paid. Amendment:

cancellations.title: Cancellation requests
cancellations.help: The Accountant asks to cancel an approved voucher that has not been paid; the Director approves or rejects it on the voucher's page.
cancellations.pendingOnly: Only those waiting for the Director

payments.title: Supplier payments
payments.help: Vouchers approved by the Director and not yet fully paid. A payment always starts from a voucher; it can never be more than what is left to pay, and saving it posts the journal entry.
payments.notPayable: This voucher is not waiting to be paid: it is not approved by the Director, already paid, or its cancellation is waiting.
payments.summary: Approved LKR {{approved}} · paid so far {{paid}} · left to pay {{remaining}}
payments.noAccount: No account can be used for this method. The Accountant links bank and cash accounts to the chart of accounts under Bank accounts.
payments.savedText: Payment {{number}} of LKR {{amount}} against voucher {{voucher}} is saved, with journal entry {{entry}}.
payments.foreignNote: {{currency}} {{left}} left to pay. It is converted at today's {{currency}} rate; the difference from the invoices' rate is posted as an exchange gain or loss.
payments.cancelPending: Cancellation asked by {{name}}: {{reason}}. Waiting for the Director.
payments.whtSummary: Withholding tax {{wht}} is kept; the payee receives {{receive}}. Enter what the payee receives.

voucherReports.title: Voucher reports
voucherReports.approvedHelp: Vouchers approved by the Director, by the date of that approval, with what has been paid.
voucherReports.pendingHelp: Vouchers waiting for approval: at which level, who can approve them, and how long since anything happened to them. Oldest first.
voucherReports.notFound: No voucher with that number that you can see.

dashboard.quotationCount: {{count}} approved or sent, no answer yet
dashboard.deliveriesDetail: {{count}} orders · {{overdue}} deliveries overdue, {{week}} due this week
dashboard.cashCompany: All bank, cash and petty cash accounts
dashboard.cashDivision: Accounts set up for this division: {{count}}

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.help: When a document has waited at one level for this many days, everyone who can approve it there is reminded again, under the bell and by email, once a day until someone acts. Each person can turn reminder emails off in My notifications.

customers.title: Customers
customers.help: Customers for quotations, proforma invoices and sales orders. A customer used on a document keeps its code and can only be deactivated, by the Sales Manager or the Director.
customers.searchHint: Name, code, VAT number or contact
customers.importHelp: One sheet named Customers, in the layout of the export. Leave Code empty for a new customer; put the code to update one. Check the file first: nothing is saved until every row is accepted.
customers.checked: The file is fine. Importing it would add {{created}} and update {{updated}} customers.
customers.sameAsBilling: Leave empty if the same as the billing address
customers.confirmDuplicate: I have checked: this is a different customer. Save anyway.

incoterms.CIP: CIP – Carriage and insurance paid to

customers.noContacts: No contacts yet. The first one added becomes the main contact.
customers.termsByAccountant: The credit limit and payment terms are changed only by the Accountant or the Director.

costing.title: Costing rates
costing.help: The rates quotation costing uses: each material's price per kg, and each division's overhead, default margin and setup rate. Machine hourly rates are kept with each machine. A rate starts today or later, so a quotation keeps the rates of its date. Kept by the Accountant.
costing.divisionHelp: Overhead is added to the direct cost (material, machine, setup, subcontract); the margin is then added to give the suggested price.
costing.removeReason: Removes a rate that has not started yet; type the reason in the Reason box first.
costing.name: Name

quotations.title: Quotations
quotations.searchHint: Number, customer, enquiry, part or drawing
quotations.breaksHelp: Optional: unit prices for other quantities (e.g. 50, 100).
quotations.worksOut: The number is given on first save. Amounts, taxes and the exchange rate of today are worked out when saved.
quotations.rateUsed: Rate used: 1 {{currency}} = LKR {{rate}} (rate of {{date}}); total LKR {{lkr}}.
quotations.noFiles: No files yet. Attach the customer's drawing for each line.
quotations.notApprovedYet: Not yet approved by the Director: it cannot be printed as final or sent to the customer.
quotations.sendForApproval: Send to the Director for approval
quotations.saveFirst: Save the draft first if you changed it.
quotations.markSent: Mark as sent to the customer
quotations.reviseHelp: A new draft with the same number and the next Rev; this one is kept as it was offered.
quotations.printsAsDraft: Prints as NOT APPROVED – DRAFT until the Director approves it.
quotations.emailFrom: From {{from}}. The quotation PDF is attached.
quotations.emailNotReady: Document email is not set up yet: ask the Admin (Settings → Document email).
quotations.emailAttachment: The quotation PDF is attached. Sending it marks the quotation Sent.
quotations.picturesHelp: Up to 3 pictures, JPG or PNG, at most 1 MB each. The approver sees them, and they can be emailed with the quotation. They can be changed only while the quotation is a draft.
quotations.pictureTooBig: {{name}} is larger than 1 MB. Make it smaller and try again.

quoteCosting.title: Costing of quotation
quoteCosting.internalOnly: Internal only: the costing is never shown to the customer.
quoteCosting.ratesOf: Rates in force on the quotation's date, {{date}}.
quoteCosting.divisionDefaults: {{division}}: overhead {{overhead}}%, margin {{margin}}%, setup LKR {{setup}} per hour.
quoteCosting.inLkr: Costing is in LKR; prices in {{currency}} use 1 {{currency}} = LKR {{rate}}.
quoteCosting.noDefaults: There are no costing rates for {{division}} on the quotation's date. Ask the Accountant to enter them (Sales → Costing rates).
quoteCosting.savedLines: The costing uses the quotation's saved lines: save the quotation first after changing quantities or prices.
quoteCosting.weightUsed: Weight used: {{kg}} kg at LKR {{rate}} per kg.
quoteCosting.subcontractHelp: Heat treatment, plating, transport and so on, in LKR. Tick “whole order” for an amount that is shared over the quantity, like a delivery.
quoteCosting.materialUsed: {{material}}: {{kg}} kg per piece at LKR {{rate}} per kg.
quoteCosting.belowCost: The price quoted is below cost for {{quantities}}.

toolingModes.separate: Charged once, as its own line

quoteCosting.noToolingLine: Add the mould as its own line on the quotation, ticked as tooling, so it is charged once.
quoteCosting.mouldingSummary: Part {{part}} g, runner {{runner}} g, {{cavities}} cavities on {{machine}}, cycle {{cycle}} s, rejects {{rejects}}%.

advances.title: Customer advances
advances.help: Money received from customers before invoicing. The Cashier records it; the Accountant approves it, and the entry is then posted (Dr bank, Cr Customer advances).
advances.record: Record and send to the Accountant
advances.recordHelp: Nothing is posted until the Accountant approves it.

proformas.title: Proforma invoices
proformas.help: Made from an accepted quotation, with its prices and terms. For the customer's advance payment, import, LC or bank documents. A proforma records no sale.
proformas.printsAsDraft: Prints as DRAFT – NOT ISSUED until it is issued.
proformas.noSale: A proforma records no sale and no receivable: nothing is posted to the accounts.
proformas.priceHelp: Prices come from the quotation for each quantity (its quantity breaks apply). Packing details print as the packing list page.
proformas.addQuotationLine: Add a line of the quotation
proformas.packingTotals: Packing: {{cartons}} cartons, net {{net}} kg, gross {{gross}} kg, {{volume}} m³
proformas.issueHelp: Once issued it cannot be changed; it can then be printed as final and emailed.

salesOrders.title: Sales orders
salesOrders.help: The customer's confirmed order, with their PO number and the delivery dates. Made from an accepted quotation or an issued proforma, or typed in for a repeat order. An order records no sale: the invoice does.
salesOrders.repeatHelp: For a repeat order with no new quotation. You type the price, so the Director approves the order before it is open. Add more lines and delivery dates on the next page.
salesOrders.directNotice: A repeat order typed in without a quotation: the Director approves its prices before it is open.
salesOrders.noSale: A sales order records no sale and no receivable; nothing is posted to the accounts.
salesOrders.directPriceHelp: Type the agreed price for each line.
salesOrders.scheduleHelp: Split a line into several deliveries (call-offs) if the customer wants it in parts. The deliveries must add up to the line's quantity.
salesOrders.actions: What to do with the order
salesOrders.confirmHelp: Needs the customer's PO number. After this the order cannot be changed.
salesOrders.sendHelp: Needs the customer's PO number. The order is open once the Director approves it.

dn.title: Delivery notes
dn.help: What leaves the factory against an open sales order. Issue the note when the goods leave: the order becomes Partly delivered, then Delivered. Print it for the customer to sign, and record the signed copy when it comes back. An issued note never changes; if it was wrong, cancel it with a reason and make a new one. Delivery notes do not change any stock until production is built (Phase 3).
dn.formHelp: Leave a line empty if none of it goes on this delivery. No line can deliver more than is still to deliver.
dn.signedCopyFile: Scan of the signed copy (PDF, JPG or PNG)
dn.actions: What to do with the delivery note
dn.print: Print for the customer to sign
dn.issueHelp: After this the note cannot be changed.

ti.title: Tax invoices
ti.help: Tax invoices in the Inland Revenue's format, made from what has been delivered. Sales or the Accountant prepare a draft; the Director, the Accountant or a salesperson given the right to issue invoices issues it, which gives it its number (for example 26NOV_W1_01) and posts it to the accounts. An issued invoice is never changed or deleted: a credit note corrects it.
ti.draftNotice: Draft: not a tax invoice yet. It gets its number when the Accountant issues it. The taxes are worked out at the rates of the invoice date.
ti.actions: What to do with the invoice
ti.issueHelp: Gives the invoice its number and posts it. After this it is never changed.
ti.accountantIssues: The invoice is issued by the Director, the Accountant or a salesperson the Admin has given the right to issue invoices.
ti.inLkr: Exchange rate {{date}}: 1 {{currency}} = LKR {{rate}}. Booked in LKR: {{amount}}.
ti.viewedYes: The customer has opened the invoice link.
ti.viewedNo: The customer has not opened the invoice link yet. The link is added to the invoice email.
ti.cardLinkHelp: When the customer asks to pay by card, make a payment link in OnePay, send it to them, and record it here. When the money arrives, record it as a card receipt.
ti.openingNote: Brought over from QuickBooks at go-live: only what was still to be paid. Its printed copy is in QuickBooks.

sa.title: Sales accounts
sa.help: The income account each division's tax invoices are credited to: one for goods and services, one for tooling (moulds and tools charged once). Changing them affects only invoices issued afterwards.

cn.title: Credit notes
cn.help: Corrections of issued tax invoices: goods returned, a price corrected or another reason. Made from the invoice by Sales or the Accountant; approved by the Director, or by a person the Admin has given the right to approve credit notes (confirmed by the Director). Approval numbers the note and posts the reverse of the invoice. A credit note never credits more than was invoiced.
cn.formHelp: Enter the amount before tax for each line credited (and, for returned goods, the quantity). The taxes are worked out at the invoice's rates when you save.
cn.actions: What to do with the credit note
cn.sendHelp: After this the credit note cannot be changed.

salesReports.title: Sales reports
salesReports.registerHelp: Every quotation by date, with its status and, once decided, why it was won or lost. Totals in LKR at each quotation's exchange rate.
salesReports.winLossHelp: Quotations won or lost in the period (by the day the outcome was recorded), with the reasons. The win rate is by number and by value.
salesReports.attentionHelp: Quotations waiting for the Director's approval, oldest first, then approved or sent quotations that expire within 7 days without an answer.
salesReports.ordersHelp: Every delivery still to make on open sales orders, by due date. Overdue deliveries are in red. The value is the delivery's share of its line, before tax.
salesReports.advancesHelp: Customer advances approved and not yet set off against invoices (from Phase 2, invoices set them off).
salesReports.winSummary: {{won}} won, {{lost}} lost: win rate {{rate}}% by number, {{valueRate}}% by value.
salesReports.noneDecided: No quotations won or lost in this period.
salesReports.noneAdvances: No advances waiting to be set off.

resets.title: Password reset
resets.help: For someone who forgot their password or lost the phone with their authenticator. The Admin asks, the Director approves, then the Admin makes a temporary password, shown once. The person must choose their own password at the next sign-in.
resets.issueHelp: Within 24 hours of approval. It is shown once; the person is signed out everywhere.
resets.shown: New temporary password for {{name}} (shown only once; give it to them privately):

noAccess.title: No access
noAccess.help: Your role does not give you access to this page. If you need it, ask the Admin.

items.title: Items
items.help: Everything SML buys and keeps or uses: resin, steel, inserts, consumables, spares and packing. A code used on a purchase order or GRN never changes; the item can then only be deactivated.
items.name: Name
items.isStock: Stock item (kept in a store and valued)
items.accountsHelp: The Accountant chooses an item's accounts; until then a stock item uses the inventory account for its category.
items.usedHelp: This item has been used on a document: its code is fixed and it can only be deactivated.
items.importHelp: One sheet named Items, in the layout of the export. Put the item code in every row: an existing code updates that item, a new one adds it. Check the file first: nothing is saved until every row is accepted.
items.checked: The file is fine. Importing it would add {{created}} and update {{updated}} items.

stores.title: Stores
stores.help: Where stock is kept, per production division. Each division has its main store, a quarantine where received goods wait for QC, and a rejected store for goods going back to the supplier. You can add more main stores.
stores.name: Name

po.title: Purchase orders
po.help: Raised by the Purchasing Officer from the item master and approved by the Director before they are sent. An approved PO never changes: revise it (it is approved again), cancel it while nothing has been received, or close it short.
po.actions: What to do with the purchase order
po.sendHelp: Needs the delivery date. After this the PO cannot be changed.
po.printsAsDraft: Prints marked DRAFT until the Director approves it.
po.emailToSupplier: Email the PO to the supplier

grn.title: Goods receipts
grn.help: What suppliers delivered against approved purchase orders. The stores person enters what arrived and confirms it; the goods then wait in the quarantine store for QC. More than the PO still expects needs the Director. A confirmed GRN never changes: a mistake is reversed, with a reason, by the Director.
grn.nothingToReceive: No approved purchase order is waiting for goods.
grn.formHelp: Enter everything that arrived in Received, including damaged goods, and how much of it is damaged. Put 0 for an item that did not come.
grn.actions: What to do with the goods receipt
grn.confirmHelp: Save your changes first. After confirming, the GRN cannot be changed; anything over the PO goes to the Director first.
grn.addPhoto: Add a photo or scan (JPG, PNG or PDF)

packageHelp.bag: One row per bag: the weight printed on the bag, then the gross weight from the scale. The bag's own weight (tare) is filled from the item if left empty.
packageHelp.coil: One row per coil: heat number, gross and tare weight from the scale.
packageHelp.bar: One row per bundle: heat number, number of bars, length of one bar in metres, and the bundle's weight. Checked against the item's kg per metre.
packageHelp.plate: One row per plate: heat number, length, width and thickness in mm, and the weight. Checked against the theoretical weight.
packageHelp.counted: One row per box: the quantity in it.

grn.tolerance: Weights more than {{pct}}% off are highlighted.
grn.savePackagesHelp: The line's received and damaged quantities become the totals of its packages. Damaged packages count as damaged.

qc.title: QC inspection
qc.help: Received goods wait in quarantine until the QC Inspector checks them against the item's inspection plan and accepts or rejects them. The person who received the goods cannot inspect them. Accepting material that fails a check needs the Director (accept under deviation).
qc.noPlan: No inspection plan for this item: record what was checked in the notes.
qc.rejectPackages: Tick the packages to reject (the rest is accepted)
qc.reason: Reason (to reject or for a deviation)
qc.askDeviation: Ask the Director to accept under deviation
qc.decideHelp: A failed critical check cannot simply be accepted. After deciding, the inspection cannot be changed.
qc.addFile: Add a certificate or photo (PDF, JPG or PNG)

plans.title: Inspection plans
plans.help: What QC checks on each item, or on every item of a category that has no plan of its own. Each check is measured (with a minimum and/or maximum) or pass/fail; a failed critical check needs the Director's approval to accept. Changing a plan does not change inspections already started.
plans.everyItemIn: Every item in {{category}} without its own plan
plans.name: Plan name

stock.title: Stock on hand
stock.help: Worked out from every stock movement, never typed. Received goods wait in quarantine at no value; when QC accepts them they move to the main store at the PO price (in LKR), and the inventory account is debited against Goods received not invoiced. Rejected and damaged goods wait in the rejected store, at no value, to go back to the supplier. Click an item to see its movements.

si.title: Supplier invoices
si.help: Supplier invoices for goods bought on purchase orders, entered by Accounts with the scan and matched three ways: each line against the goods QC accepted on the GRN and the PO's price and tax. Any difference holds the invoice until the Director approves the exception. A matched invoice is posted: Goods received not invoiced and VAT input against Accounts payable.
si.differences: Differences found by the three-way match
si.nothingOpen: No goods of this supplier and division are accepted and waiting for an invoice.
si.formHelp: Tick the goods the invoice bills and type the quantity, price and tax code exactly as printed on the invoice; the match then compares them with the GRN and the PO.
si.noScan: No scan yet: attach it before matching.
si.addScan: Attach the scan (PDF, JPG or PNG)
si.actions: What to do with the invoice
si.matchHelp: Compares every line with the GRN and the PO. If all matches, the invoice is posted and cannot be changed; otherwise it is held with the differences.
si.reopen: Back to draft to correct a typing mistake
si.askException: Ask the Director to approve the exception
si.cancel: Cancel (supplier sends a credit note or new invoice)
si.onVouchers: On payment vouchers: LKR {{amount}} · still to pay: LKR {{unpaid}}
si.setOff: Advance of LKR {{amount}} set off ({{journal}}) from voucher
si.advancesWaiting: LKR {{amount}} paid in advance on these purchase orders is not yet set off.

rtn.title: Supplier returns
rtn.help: Goods sent back to the supplier from a GRN, lot by lot. Rejected or damaged goods go back from the rejected store as soon as the stores person confirms. Goods QC had accepted need the Director: their value leaves stock against Goods received not invoiced, or with a debit note if already invoiced. Either way the purchase order expects the goods again.
rtn.acceptedHelp: Goods QC had accepted are returned only with the Director's approval. Already invoiced? A debit note reduces what is owed to the supplier.
rtn.noLots: Nothing of this kind from this GRN is in the store.
rtn.actions: What to do with the return

pr.title: Purchasing reports

help.open: Approved and partly received purchase orders, with what is still to come.
help.overdue: Open purchase orders past their delivery date.
help.grni: Goods QC accepted and the supplier has not yet invoiced, at the PO price. The total should equal the balance of the Goods received not invoiced account.
help.held: Supplier invoices held by the three-way match, and those waiting for the Director's exception.
help.exceptions: Everything the Director approved outside the normal rules: excess deliveries, QC deviations, invoice differences, returns of accepted goods and advance payments.
help.suppliers: What each supplier delivered, how much was rejected or damaged, late deliveries and returns.

pr.ledgerBalance: Balance of the Goods received not invoiced account: LKR {{amount}}
pr.waitingDetail: POs, GRN excesses, QC deviations, invoices or returns

mj.title: Manual journals
mj.help: Journals the Accountant types in, for accruals, corrections and transfers between accounts. A journal is posted to the ledger only when the Director approves it, and nobody approves their own. Suppliers are never paid by journal, only through vouchers. A posted journal never changes: reverse its entry instead.
mj.formHelp: Each line is a debit or a credit. Income and expense lines need a division; a payables line needs the supplier. Debits must equal credits before the journal can be sent.
mj.addFile: Add a document (PDF, JPG or PNG)
mj.actions: What to do with the journal
mj.sendHelp: After this the journal cannot be changed.
mj.reverseNextMonth: Accrual: reverse it automatically on the first day of the next month

rj.title: Recurring journals
rj.help: Journals that repeat, such as monthly rent or insurance accruals. On each date the ERP makes a draft journal for the Accountant who keeps the template, who checks it and sends it for approval as usual: nothing is posted without the Director. An accrual is reversed automatically on the first day of the next month. If a month is closed, no journal is made for it and the Accountant is told.
rj.name: Name
rj.formHelp: The same rules as a manual journal: debits equal credits, income and expense lines need a division, a payables line needs the supplier. Changing the template changes only the journals still to be made.

fr.title: Financial reports
fr.help: Read straight from the posted journal, so the reports always agree with each other. Choose the company or one division. Click any figure to see the ledger lines behind it; each line opens its journal entry and the document, with its scans, that posted it.

kinds.profit: Profit to date, not yet closed to retained earnings
kinds.company: Funded at company level (bank, loans and equity not held by the division)

fr.divisionNote: A division's balance sheet shows only the lines that carry the division. Bank, loans and share capital belong to the company, so the difference is shown as funded at company level.
fr.plNote: Income is shown positive and costs negative, so the total is the profit. Comparisons with last year and the budget come with the budgets task.
fr.glNote: Balances are debit minus credit: a credit balance shows as a negative figure. Lines of merged accounts are shown under the account that replaced them.

cf.difference: The statement does not add up to the change in cash by LKR {{amount}}. Tell the Accountant.
cf.note: Indirect method, for the whole company: the period's profit, with depreciation added back, adjusted by the change in each balance sheet account. Cash means the bank, cash and petty cash accounts. A negative figure is cash used, for example more owed to us by customers or a machine bought.

os.title: Opening stock
os.help: The stores counted at go-live, with the cost of each item, loaded from Excel by the Accountant. Nothing goes into stock until the Director approves; then the quantities go into the main stores and their value is posted (Inventory against Opening balance equity). Only for items that have not yet moved in that store.
os.template: Download the Excel sheet to fill in
os.loadAgain: Load the sheet again (replaces the lines)
os.checked: The file is fine: {{rows}} rows, LKR {{value}}.
os.actions: What to do with the opening stock
os.sendHelp: After this it cannot be changed.

taxRates.title: Tax rates
taxRates.help: The rates of VAT and SSCL used on quotations, proformas, POs, invoices and vouchers. SSCL has a rate for each kind of supply: manufactured goods (SSCL-M), services (SSCL) and resold goods (SSCL-R); all print as SSCL. When the government changes a rate, the Admin or the Accountant enters the new rate from its date; it applies only after the Director confirms it. Documents already made keep the rate of their date.
taxRates.proposeHelp: The new rate starts on its date once the Director confirms; if confirmed later, it starts on the day of confirmation.

receipts.title: Customer receipts
receipts.help: Money received for tax invoices. The Cashier records it and splits it over the customer's invoices; the Accountant approves it and it is posted (Dr bank, Cr the customer's receivable). A cheque waits in Undeposited funds until it is banked; a post-dated cheque is posted on its date.
receipts.nothingOpen: No customer has an open invoice.
receipts.chequeHelp: A cheque goes to Undeposited funds until it is deposited. If it is dated later, it is posted on that date.
receipts.recordHelp: The split must add up to the amount. Nothing is posted until the Accountant approves it. Record any extra as an advance.
receipts.postDatedHelp: Approved. The cheque is posted on {{date}}.
receipts.currencyNote: Amounts in {{currency}}. The money goes into a {{currency}} account; any exchange difference is posted when approved.

ar.title: Receivables and statements
ar.help: What each customer owes on its invoices, by days past the due date, next to its ledger balance. Only approved receipts count as paid here. Open a customer for its statement.
ar.onHold: On credit hold: new sales orders and invoices need the Director's allowance.
ar.remindersOn: On: the statement is emailed to {{to}} every {{days}} days while invoices are overdue (sent as {{by}}).
ar.sendReminders: Email reminders while invoices are overdue

holds.title: Credit holds
holds.help: Sales orders and tax invoices stopped because the customer has overdue invoices or would go over its credit limit. Each one goes ahead only when the Director allows it.

ap.title: Payables and supplier statements
ap.help: What we owe each supplier, by days past the due date: matched supplier invoices and invoices on vouchers, less advances set off, debit notes and what has been paid. Click a supplier for its items.
ap.statementsHelp: Type in a supplier's statement or import it (Excel or CSV with Date, Reference, Description, Debit, Credit). The ERP matches each line to our invoices, debit notes and payments and lists the differences.
ap.ourBalance: What we owe in our books
ap.importHelp: Importing fills the lines below; check them, then save.
ap.theirsOnly: On their statement, not in our books
ap.oursOnly: In our books, not on their statement

reorder.title: Reorder levels
reorder.help: Each item's reorder level and quantity per main store. When what is in the store plus what is already ordered or requested falls to the level, the stores person and purchasing are told, and one click raises a purchase request.
reorder.lowOnly: Only those at or below their level
reorder.noneLow: Nothing is at its reorder level.
reorder.low: At or below its reorder level
reorder.setHelp: Saving for an item and store that already has a level changes it.
reorder.lastSupplier: The supplier of the last order

prq.title: Purchase requests
prq.help: Requests to buy, raised by the stores person or purchasing. Once approved, purchasing makes each one into a draft purchase order, which goes for its own approval.
prq.makeOrderHelp: A draft purchase order is made for the supplier chosen, at the last price paid to them unless you type a price. It then goes to the Director for approval as usual.

cheques.title: Cheque register
cheques.help: Our cheques and the customers' cheques in one place. Customers' cheques wait in Undeposited funds until they are put on a deposit slip. Mark a cheque cleared when the bank shows it; a customer's cheque that comes back unpaid is returned, which puts the money back on the customer's account and opens the invoices again. Transfers between our own accounts are Internal Transfer vouchers.
cheques.depositHelp: Tick the cheques taken to the bank together. The bank is debited and Undeposited funds credited.
cheques.nothingInHand: No cheques are waiting to be deposited.

bs.title: Bank statements
bs.help: Import the bank's statement file (Excel, CSV, or a PDF with text) with the bank's template. The file is read and checked first: every balance must follow from the one before, so a misread file is refused. Lines already imported from an earlier statement are skipped.
bs.templatesHelp: How each bank's file is laid out. For Excel or CSV, type the column headings exactly as in the file; for a PDF, nothing more is needed. Tick 'checked' once a real file has imported correctly.

columns.amount_column: One signed amount heading (instead of out and in)

bs.checkedLabel: Checked with a real file from the bank

rec.title: Bank reconciliation
rec.help: Match each line of the bank's statement to its payment, deposit, receipt or transfer in the books; post bank charges and interest from the line in one click. Nothing is matched or posted without your click. When every line is in the books and the difference is nil, finish the month: it is then locked.
rec.unpresented: In the books, not yet on the statement
rec.notInBooks: On the statement, not yet in the books
rec.noStatement: No statement imported up to this date
rec.noCandidates: Nothing in the books has this amount near this date.
rec.rulesHelp: When a line's description contains these words, its posting account is suggested (for example "SERVICE CHARGE" to bank charges).

petty.title: Petty cash
petty.help: The custodian records each small expense with a photo of its slip; nothing is posted then. The Clerk tops the float up with a Petty Cash voucher listing the expenses, which goes through the three approvals; paying it posts the expenses and the float is whole again.
petty.none: You hold no petty cash, and there is none to see.
petty.cashInHand: Cash that should be in the box
petty.topUpHelp: {{amount}} of expenses are waiting. A draft Petty Cash voucher is made with one line per expense and its slip; check it and submit it.

sw.title: Stores work
sw.help: Material issued to a division or section and returned, at the weighted average cost; adjustments and write-offs, which the Director approves before anything moves; and stock counts, whose differences go to the Director.
sw.costIfNew: Cost per unit (only for an item never held)
sw.countHelp: The sheet lists what the books say per item and lot today. Type what is counted (0 for what is not there); submitting sends the differences to the Director.

fa.title: Fixed assets
fa.help: The register of the company's assets, monthly depreciation worked out for the Accountant to check and then posted, and disposals with their gain or loss. Each class's method and rate are agreed with the auditors and entered under Classes; until then that class is not depreciated.
fa.name: Name
fa.classesHelp: Enter each class's method and yearly rate as the auditors agree. A new rate applies from the month given; months already posted keep the rate they used.
fa.noRate: No method and rate yet: not depreciated

tax.title: Tax reports
tax.help: The month's VAT return, SSCL and withholding tax, for filing. Supplies and output VAT come from the issued tax invoices less credit notes, by the tax code on each line; exports are shown apart as zero-rated. Input VAT is what the books claimed. Every line links to its document; download Excel or PDF for the filing.
tax.ledgerDiffers: The VAT payable account shows {{ledger}} for the month: check entries posted to it by hand.

reval.title: Month-end revaluation
reval.help: At each month end, what is still open in a foreign currency is valued again at that day's exchange rate: customer and supplier invoices not yet settled, and the bank and cash accounts held in a foreign currency. The invoices' difference is an unrealised gain or loss, reversed on the first day of the next month; the bank balances keep their new value. Check the month, then post it.
reval.balancesHelp: The balance of each foreign-currency account on the last day of the month, in its own currency. It is filled in from the month's imported bank statement; type it if there is none.
reval.openItemsTotal: Open invoices: unrealised gain (loss is negative)
reval.balancesTotal: Bank and cash: exchange gain (loss is negative)
reval.nothing: Nothing is open in a foreign currency at this month end.

budget.title: Budgets
budget.help: Each financial year's budget by account, division and month. The Accountant prepares it on this page or imports it from Excel, and the Director approves it. An approved budget never changes: a revision is a new version, which replaces it once approved. The profit and loss then shows the budget next to the actual.
budget.startHelp: If the year already has an approved budget, the new version starts as a copy of it.
budget.heading: Budget {{label}}, version {{version}}
budget.gridOf: Budget {{label}} by account, division and month
budget.gridHelp: Type income and costs as positive amounts. Leave a month empty for nothing budgeted.
budget.importHelp: Use the Excel download as the layout: Account (number or name), Division (WS, IM, HO), then one column per month. Importing replaces this draft's amounts; if any row is wrong, nothing changes and every problem is listed.
budget.reasonOrComment: Comment, or the reason for returning or rejecting
budget.saveFirst: Save your changes before sending it.
budget.plNote: Budget: the approved budget for the months of the period. Difference: actual less budget, so a positive figure is better than budget (more income or lower costs); % is the difference as a share of the budget.

close.title: Month-end and year-end close
close.help: Before the Director closes a month, its checklist must be complete. The system checks what it can see; the Accountant marks the rest done with a note. Once all twelve months are closed, the Director closes the year: its profit goes to retained earnings and the next year starts from nil.
close.notReady: The Director can close the month once every item is done.
close.accrualsHint: What was accrued or prepaid, e.g. electricity JNL-0004
close.otherHint: How it was done, or why it is not needed this month
close.yearHelp: Closing a year posts one entry on the first day of the next year that moves every income and cost account's balance to retained earnings. The closed year's profit and loss report does not change. The Director can reopen the year with a reason; the entry is then reversed.
close.yearReady: every month is closed; the year can be closed
close.historyLine: Closed by {{by}}: entry {{entry}} on {{date}}, profit LKR {{profit}}.

planner.title: Cash flow planner
planner.help: The company's bank and cash balance, projected day by day for the next 13 weeks: what customers owe (on the due date, moved by how late each customer usually pays), cheques received, what we owe suppliers (on the due date, or today if overdue) and recurring payments. Add "what-if" items to see their effect; they are never posted. Payroll will be added with the payroll module.
planner.shortfall: The balance goes below nil on {{day}}. Plan a receipt, delay a payment or arrange an overdraft.
planner.whatIfsHelp: Untick an item to see the projection without it. Items are never posted.

rb.title: Report builder
rb.help: Build your own report: start from a data source or a ready-made report, choose the columns and drag them into order, add filters, group with subtotals, sort, and spread an amount over months or divisions. Save it, share it with a role, download it in Excel or PDF, or email it. Everyone sees only what their own access and divisions allow.
rb.dragHelp: Drag the columns into order, or use the arrows.
rb.name: Report name
rb.truncated: Only the first {{count}} rows are shown. Add a filter to narrow it down.

mig.title: Opening balances from QuickBooks
mig.help: At go-live, upload QuickBooks' own Excel exports as they come out of QuickBooks. They are checked first: the trial balance must balance, every account, customer and supplier must be found, and the open invoices and bills must add up to the debtors and creditors. When all is in order, one opening entry is made for the Director to approve. Stock is loaded on Stores → Opening stock, and fixed assets on Fixed assets.

file.items: Item list (to compare the stock value)

mig.allGood: Everything agrees. You can make the opening balances.
mig.comment: Comment, or the reason for returning or rejecting
mig.part2Help: After the opening balances are posted, upload the same A/R and A/P ageing files again. Each open invoice and bill is brought over for what is still open, so receipts and vouchers after go-live are matched to them. Payments and credits not yet applied in QuickBooks are taken off the oldest. Each customer and supplier must agree with their opening balance.
mig.defaultDivision: Division for bills and invoices with no class
mig.checkItems: Check the open invoices and bills

par.title: Parallel run: compare with QuickBooks
par.help: During the parallel month, enter the same transactions in both systems. At the month end, upload QuickBooks' trial balance (and its A/R and A/P ageing) as at that date. Every account, customer and supplier is compared with the ERP at the same date, and each difference is listed to explain. Nothing is posted; compare as often as you like.
par.showAll: Show the lines that agree too

emp.title: Employees
emp.help: Everyone employed by the company. HR adds and keeps employees here or from Excel; the Director sees them too. The employee number never changes, and an employee who leaves is kept with their leaving date, never deleted. A new or changed salary bank account is checked by the Director before salary is paid to it.
emp.bankPendingOnly: Bank account waiting for a check
emp.addHelp: The other details and the bank account can be added on the employee's page after saving.
emp.importHelp: Fill in the template, one row per employee. Existing employees are updated by their employee number. The file is checked first; if any row is wrong nothing is saved and every wrong row is listed.
emp.checked: The file is correct: {{added}} to add and {{updated}} to update. Press Import to save.
emp.leftOn: Left on {{date}}: {{reason}}. The record is kept as it was.
emp.bankChangedBy: Entered or changed by {{name}} on {{at}}. Confirm it with the employee before salary is paid to it.
emp.bankWaiting: Waiting for the Director to check it.
emp.bankReason: Reason for changing the bank account
emp.leaveHelp: The employee is then shown under Left and can no longer be changed.
emp.consentMissing: The employee has not agreed to the location check yet, so cannot clock in.
emp.requestBank: A new salary account: after approval it waits for the Director's check.

pc.title: Pay components
pc.help: The earnings and deductions on payslips. Each earning says whether it counts for EPF and ETF and whether it is taxable for APIT; check these with the Accountant. Fixed components have a monthly amount on each employee's page; those entered each month are typed in with the payroll. A component's code and kind never change; one no longer used is marked so, never deleted. A payroll keeps the settings it was run with. An employee has at most four allowances.
pc.name: Name
pc.flagsHelp: A deduction never counts for EPF or APIT.

pay.title: Pay
pay.net: Fixed pay after deductions, each month
pay.totalsHelp: Of this, LKR {{epf}} counts for EPF and ETF and LKR {{apit}} for APIT. Overtime, amounts entered each month, EPF and APIT are added by the payroll.
pay.changesHelp: Every new employee's pay and every change is prepared by HR and takes effect only when the Director approves it. The person who prepared it never approves it.
pay.amountsHelp: Leave an amount blank to keep it as it is; 0 stops a component. An employee has at most four allowances. The attendance bonus (default LKR 1,500) is lost for a pay month with four half days absent.
pay.withSettings: Also set this employee's own overtime, leave and APIT settings
pay.settingsHelp: Leave a box blank to use the default: the division's work rule, or the leave of the employee's category.
pay.comment: Comment (the reason when returning or rejecting)

s.casual_leave_days: Casual and sick leave (days a year)

hol.title: Holidays and leave types
hol.help: The year's public, bank, mercantile, Poya and company holidays, and the kinds of leave with the days granted each year. Holidays and Sundays are not counted as leave days. A holiday that has passed is kept as it was.
hol.name: Name
hol.none: No holidays entered for this year.

lt.title: Leave types
lt.help: Annual and casual leave follow the Shop and Office Employees Act: no annual leave in the year of joining, then 14, 10, 7 or 4 days the next year by the quarter of joining; casual leave half a day for each completed month in the year of joining. Check the Wages Board's rules for factory staff with the Accountant. Unused leave is not carried forward unless a maximum is set.
lt.name: Name
lt.wbRule: Wages Board: how the days are granted

leave.title: Leave
leave.help: Leave recorded by HR from the approved leave form, and leave applied for by employees, which HR approves. Days are Monday to Saturday, not holidays. Leave is cancelled, never deleted.
leave.grantHelp: Gives every working employee the year's annual and casual leave by the rules, and any days carried forward. Run it once at the start of the year; running it again adds only what is missing, for example for new joiners.
leave.recordHelp: Leave with a balance cannot be more than the days left.

att.title: Attendance
att.help: Attendance comes from the Excel sheet HR fills in: one row per employee and day, with times in and out, the shift, a leave code for a day of leave, and remarks. A later sheet replaces the same days until HR confirms the pay month. Payroll uses confirmed pay months only.
att.uploadHelp: The file is checked first; if any row is wrong nothing is saved and every wrong row is listed. A leave code with no times is a day of leave; with times, half a day.
att.checked: The file is correct: {{rows}} rows for {{employees}} employees ({{months}}). Press Save.
att.confirmedBy: Confirmed by {{name}} on {{at}}. The days are fixed; the leave codes are recorded as leave.
att.confirmHelp: When the pay month has ended and the sheet is complete, confirm it. The leave codes are then recorded as leave (balances are checked) and the days can no longer change.

ot.title: Overtime
ot.help: Each employee's pay month from the confirmed attendance, worked out by the division's work rules: overtime on working days (beyond the shift or normal day), on Sundays and on holidays; short time (late beyond the grace period, or left early), covered by short leave up to the number allowed; the rest is no-pay time. Days absent and unpaid leave are no-pay days. The section's supervisor or the Director checks each month; payroll pays the checked figures. Short leave is paid for Shop and Office staff; for Wages Board staff each one costs a quarter of a day's pay.
ot.notConfirmed: HR has not confirmed this pay month's attendance yet; the figures may still change and cannot be checked.
ot.ruleLine: Rules: {{day}} hours a day; overtime {{working}} times on working days, {{sunday}} on Sundays, {{holiday}} on holidays; {{grace}} minutes' grace.
ot.none: No employees for you to check in this division.

wr.title: Work rules
wr.help: Each division's working-time and overtime rules from a month on. A new rule never changes earlier months; a rule whose month has not come can be withdrawn. Until the owner confirms them (backlog question 5): 8 hours a day; overtime 1.5 times on working days and 2 times on Sundays and holidays; 10 minutes' grace; 2 short leaves of up to 90 minutes a month; overtime from 30 minutes in 15-minute steps; hourly rate = monthly pay ÷ 240.
wr.addHelp: Fields left empty keep the values of the rule in force.

pp.title: Pay period
pp.help: Salaries are paid for a pay month: by default the 21st of one month to the 20th of the next (pay month November = 21 October to 20 November), paid on the last day of the month. Attendance, overtime, short leave and no-pay are worked out per pay month.
pp.startDayHelp: The day of the month before the pay month on which it starts (1 = the calendar month).
pp.addHelp: A new pay period starts from a pay month whose previous pay month is not confirmed in any division, and never changes earlier months.

payroll.title: Payroll
payroll.help: HR prepares a division's payroll for a pay month once attendance is confirmed and every employee's overtime is checked. Each figure shows where it came from. The Director approves it (never the person who prepared it); then it is locked.
payroll.prepareHelp: Earnings come from the approved pay settings; overtime and no-pay from the checked figures; EPF 8% and 12%, ETF 3%; APIT from the IRD table.
payroll.enterHelp: For amounts that change each month (an incentive, an advance recovery). 0 removes it. The payroll is worked out again.
payroll.comment: Comment (the reason when returning or rejecting)
payroll.posted: Approved as {{number}} and posted to the accounts (journal {{journal}}): salaries and wages, the company's EPF and ETF, and EPF, ETF, APIT, deductions and net salaries payable. To pay the net LKR {{net}}, the Clerk enters a salary voucher coded to Salaries payable; it goes through the Accountant and the Director as usual.
payroll.payslipsHelp: Print them (one page each) or email each employee's payslip to their email address. An emailed payslip opens with the employee's NIC number as its password; no copy goes to the company mailbox. Every email is recorded.
payroll.labourPerHour: Labour cost: LKR {{rate}} an hour ({{hours}} hours worked)
payroll.labourNoHours: Labour cost per hour: no hours worked in attendance
payroll.labourHelp: Gross pay plus the company's EPF 12% and ETF 3% (LKR {{cost}}), over the hours worked in attendance. Job costing uses it per section.

taxTables.title: APIT tables and EPF rates
taxTables.help: The IRD's APIT tables and the EPF and ETF rates the payroll uses, each from a date. Table 01 (primary employment) is entered from the IRD's tables for 2025/26, which apply until the IRD issues new ones. Enter Table 07 (secondary employment) before paying anyone under it. A table in force never changes; enter a new one from a later date.
taxTables.addHelp: Tax = monthly earnings × rate − the amount in 'less', in the first band the earnings do not pass. The last band has no upper limit.

returns.title: Statutory returns
returns.help: EPF, ETF and APIT returns from the approved payrolls, for the paper or online forms: view, download as Excel or PDF. A division whose payroll is not approved yet is named under the return.
returns.none: Nobody in an approved payroll for this period.

credits.title: Advances and loans
credits.help: HR records each salary advance or loan; the Director approves every one. The Clerk pays it by a voucher coded to Staff loans and advances. The payroll recovers an advance in full in its pay month and a loan in equal monthly instalments, never leaving the employee 40% of the basic salary or less (what it cannot take waits for the next month). A leaver repays the balance from the final salary as far as it goes.
credits.recordHelp: It is refused if the first recovery would leave the employee 40% of the basic salary or less.

my.title: My pay and leave
my.applyHelp: Your section's supervisor or HR approves it. You can withdraw it until then.
my.detailsHelp: Change what is wrong and ask HR to update it. A new salary account is used only after the Director's check.

clock.title: Clock in and out
clock.sitesHelp: You can clock in or out only at a site: {{sites}}.
clock.consent: I agree that my phone's location is checked when I press Clock in or Clock out (only at that moment, never otherwise).
clock.noLocation: Your phone did not share its location. Allow location for this site in the browser, then try again.

punch.bringInHelp: Bring the pay month's clock-ins and clock-outs from phones into attendance. Days entered from a sheet are kept; a clock-in without a clock-out is listed for you to enter in the sheet; today waits for tomorrow.
punch.checked: {{punches}} punches make {{days}} days for {{employees}} employees. Check them, then bring them in.
punch.saved: {{days}} days for {{employees}} employees brought into attendance.
punch.sitesHelp: Employees set to 'Only at a site' can clock in only within a site's radius. Copy the latitude and longitude from a map (long-press the place in Google Maps).
